en: I will call you back after the meeting.
tamil: மீட்டிங் முடிஞ்சதும் நான் உங்களுக்கு திரும்ப கூப்பிடுறேன்.
context: Telling a caller you are busy right now.
explain: 'Call back' means return a phone call. 'After the meeting' tells when.

en: Do you have a minute to talk?
context: Approaching a colleague or boss for a quick chat.
explain: 'Do you have a minute' is a polite way to start a short talk. It does not mean exactly sixty seconds.

en: My boss is giving me too much work.
tamil: என் பாஸ் எனக்கு ரொம்ப அதிகமா வேலை குடுக்கிறார்.
context: Complaining to a close friend about workload.
explain: 'Is giving' shows something happening these days. 'Too much' means more than you can handle.

en: I have attached the document for your reference.
context: Writing a line in an email with a file.
explain: 'Have attached' is common in emails. 'For your reference' means so that you can look at it.

en: Could you please resend the invoice?
tamil: இன்வாய்ஸை தயவு செஞ்சு திரும்ப அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a vendor or client to send a bill again.
explain: 'Resend' means send again. Adding 'please' makes the request polite.

en: The server was down all morning.
tamil: சர்வர் காலையில இருந்து முழுக்க வேலை செய்யல.
context: Explaining why work was delayed.
explain: 'Was down' means not working. 'All morning' shows it lasted the whole morning.

en: I have never worked night shifts before.
tamil: நான் இதுக்கு முன்னாடி நைட் ஷிஃப்ட்ல வேலை பாத்ததே இல்ல.
context: Telling HR about your experience.
explain: 'Have never worked' talks about life experience up to now. 'Before' makes it stronger.

en: I am sorry, I missed your message.
context: Apologising for a late reply.
explain: 'I am sorry' is a simple apology. 'Missed' here means did not see it.

en: Let me check with my team first.
context: Buying time before answering a client.
explain: 'Let me' tells the other person you will do something. 'Check with' means ask someone.

alt.en: Let me confirm with my team and get back to you.

en: We should plan the work before we start.
context: Giving advice in a team discussion.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'Before we start' links two actions in order.

en: He did not attend the training session.
context: Telling HR who was absent.
explain: 'Did not' is followed by the base verb 'attend'. We do not add -ed after 'did not'.

en: Is the printer working again?
context: Asking a colleague before printing.
explain: 'Is working' asks about the present condition. 'Again' shows it was broken earlier.

en: I will be on a call till noon.
tamil: நான் மதியம் வரைக்கும் ஒரு காலில் இருப்பேன்.
context: Telling a teammate you are not free.
explain: 'Will be' shows a state in the future. 'Till noon' means until twelve o'clock.

en: Your performance review is next week.
context: A manager reminding an employee.
explain: A review checks how well you worked. We use the present for a planned event.

en: Can I get a copy of the schedule?
context: Asking the team lead for the plan.
explain: 'Can I get' is an easy, polite way to ask for something. 'Schedule' means a plan with times.

en: I have been in this company for five years.
tamil: நான் இந்த கம்பெனியில அஞ்சு வருஷமா இருக்கேன்.
context: Introducing yourself in an interview or meeting.
explain: 'Have been' with 'for' shows how long something has continued. It still goes on now.

en: Please submit your timesheet by Friday.
context: HR or manager giving a reminder.
explain: 'Submit' means hand in. 'By Friday' means not later than Friday.

en: They are interviewing three candidates today.
tamil: அவங்க இன்னைக்கு மூணு பேரை இன்டர்வியூ பண்றாங்க.
context: Explaining why the hiring team is busy.
explain: 'Are interviewing' shows something happening around now. 'Candidates' are people applying for a job.

en: Thank you for your quick help.
context: Thanking a colleague by email or in person.
explain: A short, polite thank-you line. 'Quick' means fast, so it praises their speed.

en: Will you be joining the team lunch tomorrow?
context: Inviting a colleague to a group lunch.
explain: 'Will you be joining' is a polite way to ask about future plans. It sounds softer than 'Will you join'.

en: I cannot finish this without your help.
tamil: உங்க உதவி இல்லாம என்னால இதை முடிக்க முடியாது.
context: Asking a senior for support.
explain: 'Cannot' shows inability. 'Without' means if you are not there to help.
